summary: Josho Nozawa was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Susumu Yamaguchi. He held a professorship at Koyasan University, attested in 1950.
Linguist Joshua T. Katz studied at the Dalton School, Yale (~1987–1991), Oxford (~1991–1993), and Harvard (~1993–1998). He served on the faculty at Princeton University from 1998 to 2022.
Scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology Joshua W. C. Cutler studied under Geshe Wangyal. He held a post at the Tibetan Buddhist Learning Center, attested in 2004.

Philosopher Josiah Royce studied at the University of California, Berkeley (~1871–1875) and Johns Hopkins University (~1876–1878). He taught at UC Berkeley (~1878–1882) and held a long-standing post at Harvard University (~1882–1916).

Scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology José Ignacio Cabezón studied at Caltech, Sera and Sera Jey Monasteries, and UW–Madison (PhD 1986) under Geshe Lhundub Sopa. He taught at Iliff School of Theology (~1990–2001) and UC Santa Barbara (2001).
Working in Buddhist and religious studies, Jotika Khur-Yearn completed a PhD at SOAS University of London under doctoral supervisor Kate Crosby (attested 2012).

Scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology Jowita Kramer earned her MA and doctorate at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen, and habilitated at LMU Munich. She held posts at Oxford, UC Berkeley, Heidelberg, Göttingen, EPHE, and Munich.

Joy Brennan, a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies, earned a PhD at the University of Chicago, where she studied under Paul Mendes-Flohr, Richard Rosengarten, and Constance Furey, in addition to Diane Martin.
Juan Wu is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who earned a PhD at Cardiff University under the supervision of Max Deeg, attested in 2012.

Indologist Judit Törzsök studied at Eötvös Loránd University and the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson (DPhil 1999). She held posts at the University of Lille (associate professor 2001) and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (professor from 2018).

Judith Simmer-Brown, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studied at Western Washington University and with Chögyam Trungpa and Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche. In 1977, she became chair of the Religious Studies Department at Naropa University.

Juhn Y. Ahn, a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, earned his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley in 2007. By 2019, he held a post as Associate Professor of Buddhist and Korean Studies at the University of Michigan.
Juhyung Rhi, a scholar in Buddhist studies and art history, earned his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley. In 1992, he became Professor of Art History at Seoul National University.
Juichiro Tanabe, working in religious studies, pursued postgraduate and PhD studies at the University of Bradford between 2000 and 2010. He also studied under Richard Hunn.

A scholar of philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies, Jules Barthélemy-Saint-Hilaire studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand and Bourbon College. He served as Professor of Greek at the Collège de France (1838–1852) and belonged to the Académie des Sciences Morales et Politiques.

Indologist and linguist Jules Bloch studied at Lycée Charlemagne, the University of Paris, ENLOV, and the EPHE. He held posts at the EPHE, ENLOV, the University of Lyon, and the Collège de France (1936–1951).

Trained in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Levinson earned a PhD from the University of Virginia (1994) under Jeffrey Hopkins and studied with several Tibetan masters. He held a post at Hamline University in 1996 and founded the Light of Berotsana Translation Group.

Historian Jules Michelet studied at Lycée Charlemagne (1812–1816). He held posts at Collège-lycée Jacques-Decour (1822), École Normale Supérieure (1827), Archives nationales (1830–1852), and the Collège de France (1838–1852).

Scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and Sinological studies Jules Mohl studied at the University of Tübingen and under Silvestre de Sacy and Abel-Rémusat. He taught at Tübingen (1826) and served at the Société Asiatique and Collège de France (1847–1876).

Scholar of history, archaeology, linguistics, and Indology Jules Oppert studied at Heidelberg, Bonn, Berlin, and Kiel (~1844–1847). He served as a professor at the Collège de France from 1874 to 1905.
